originality.rationale: The published finite-lattice criterion in Chen–Li–Huang is only sufficient and concerns the first derivative at zero; the all-rate global no-benefit converse and strict boundary follow from a positive-coefficient Chebyshev comparison. Bonomo–Pal and Radice et al. use different resetting clocks; bounded-domain continuum arguments do not prove this discrete finite grid inequality. Full accessible primary paper sections, figures, appendices/conclusions and published-finding corpus/own history were inspected. A semantically equivalent prior coefficient inequality is a residual risk.
residual_risks: Earlier work may contain the equivalent positivity-of-Chebyshev-coefficients all-rate converse in a different field or terminology.
Independent mathematical review and exhaustive historical-priority research have not been performed.

value.rationale: A useful sharp phase diagram for a canonical finite first-passage Markov process eliminates otherwise necessary global reset-rate searches and settles whether a failed local rate test could miss a beneficial intermediate rate, explicitly including the degenerate first derivative boundary.
